## TL;DR I ran a headless WebKit QA pass over the update banner, the release notes modal, the installed-version restart notice and the sidebar version label at 375, 768 and 1280 px. The pass found four product defects and one fixture defect. All are fixed with regression tests. The restart and dismiss flows were verified only against fixtures: the restart POST is intercepted and faked, and no real server was restarted. The QA record is `docs/qa/2026-11-update-banner-qa.md`, and the harness is `docs/qa/measure-update-banner.mjs`. ## Work and rationale The task asked for a QA pass with fixes, so I started by reading the component's script and template. Four states needed coverage: supervised, hand-run, failure and dismissed. Existing shot fixtures already cover `release:updateAvailable`, `restartPending` (light and dark), `restartProgress` and `restartError`, but none covers the hand-run state, and none drives a real click through the dismiss paths. I therefore wrote a harness modelled on the #1225 toasts pass: it serves the built SPA from a throwaway fixture root through `ui-harness`, runs headless WebKit, and intercepts the four update endpoints in the page. The restart POST is recorded and faked, which keeps the acceptance criterion "never restart a real server" true by construction. Each scenario gets a fresh browser context. The harness ran 126 checks on the first pass, with 18 failures. I sorted the failures before changing any product code. Six were copy defects: the restart notice linked "#0214" as its only reference, and the hand-run copy used the phrase "serve flags". Three were the failure fixture showing "Run in a terminal." with no command, because the fixture omitted `restartCommand`. The real status route always sends that field, so the defect is in the fixture, but its capture was misleading and I fixed it. The other nine were harness artifacts: a modal assertion that read `innerText` (which uppercases "Installed"), page errors from reload-aborted requests that WebKit reports as "due to access control checks", and the deliberate 500 in the failure scenario. I fixed the harness for those and left the product unchanged. The product fixes were small and targeted. The restart copy now says "same settings and port it was started with" and links "Read more on GitHub". The active-work sentence says "are running", and its pluralization test expects that. The waiting line is now a muted `

` with a full-row flex rule, matching the alert; before, it was an unstyled span at body size in both layouts, which I confirmed visually at 375 px. Release-note lists now set `list-style` explicitly, because the global list reset had removed the bullets. The restart failure fixture now includes its command. I did not change the sidebar version label. It was not visible at 375 or 768 in the run, and the installed version still appears in the restart notice title and in the release modal at every width. I recorded it as an observation. ## Approaches tried I first considered a single shot-based check, using the existing `release:*` fixtures for every state. It was quick, but it could not cover hand-run, because no fixture sets `supervisorKind: none`, and it could not click through dismiss. I switched to route interception for the update endpoints and kept the fixtures for the failure capture. That gave full control over the restart response and let the POST body be asserted. I also considered asserting the copy through a mount test only; I kept that as regression coverage, but the browser run was needed to see the layout defects. For the harness itself, I first counted every `console` error. That produced fixture access-control noise and the intended 500, so I narrowed the check to uncaught `pageerror` events, with a comment explaining why. I also considered faking the restart at the server level instead; I rejected that because the browser-side route is the one the component actually calls. ## Challenges and blockers The biggest challenge was separating product defects from harness noise, since the first run failed 18 times. Reading each failure against the screenshot resolved it. A second challenge was that `innerText` applies CSS `text-transform`, so the modal check failed on case alone. Switching to `textContent` fixed it, and the regex now tolerates the missing space between the label and the version. There is one real limit: the restart behaviour is verified only against fixtures. "Restart now" proves the UI sends the request and shows the accepted state. It does not prove that a service manager or a hand-run server comes back. The acceptance criterion forbids a real restart here, so a human should run one real hand-run restart on a disposable server if that proof is needed. I have not claimed it. Two items are outside this task's scope and I did not change them. The top bar's "New version available" button calls `repo.restartServer()` directly, with no dialog, no "Restart when idle" and no dismiss. I have noted it as a candidate for a follow-up task. The uncertain-supervisor state is covered by an existing mount test rather than by this browser pass. ## Key learnings - A failing harness run is only useful if each failure is classified against a screenshot. Here the classification found that 9 of 18 failures were in the harness, which I would have missed by fixing assertions blindly. - Copy that reads fine to the author can still be wrong for a user. "serve flags" and an issue number as a link are internal vocabulary. A regression test that greps for them is cheap insurance. - A fixture can hide a real layout bug. The empty command in the failure capture was a fixture gap, but it would have shipped unnoticed if the fixture had been trusted as the real data. - Computed-style assertions (font size, `list-style-type`) catch defects that text assertions cannot. The waiting line and the bullets both passed every text check and only failed on style. ## Generated change summary Base tree: `82d089e6efa21568a0d0bfea30b23ba43dfabbde` Source tree: `79f3a07e1f6e5a9aed5e69b402d09972e7082575` - A docs/qa/2026-11-update-banner-qa.md: +114 / −0 - A docs/qa/measure-update-banner.mjs: +599 / −0 - M src/ui-app/src/components/ReleaseUpdateNotification.vue: +27 / −10 - M src/ui-app/tests/releases.test.ts: +56 / −4
